s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis
salient_findings: Reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
Vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
key_facts: 5-year history of lesion
Spontaneous onset with no previous trauma
No improvement with topical antifungal cream
No local lymphadenopathy
Negative for HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
Poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation
Prominent hemosiderin deposits on Perls Prussian blue staining

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis and histologic findings of poorly defined vascular proliferation and prominent hemosiderin deposits

shortlist.label: Hobnail hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similar histologic features, including poorly defined vascular channels and bland endothelial cells, and is a plausible diagnosis given the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by similar histologic features, including vascular channels and spindle-shaped endothelial cells, and could be considered in the differential diagnosis

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Although rare, this entity matches some histologic features, such as poorly defined vascular channels, and should be retained as a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Papillary intralymphatic angioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Given the clinical presentation and histologic findings, including vascular proliferation and endothelial cell characteristics, this diagnosis remains plausible

shortlist.label: Acquired tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered due to the presence of vascular proliferation and the potential for gradual enlargement of the lesion

shortlist.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely due to the lack of systemic symptoms and distinct histologic features, this diagnosis cannot be entirely ruled out without further evaluation

shortlist.label: Dabska tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Remains a possible diagnosis due to the presence of vascular channels and endothelial cell characteristics, despite being a rare entity

raw.rationale: The presence of a reddish hematomalike plaque with a brownish peripheral border, prominent hemosiderin deposits, and poorly defined vascular proliferation are characteristic features of targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.

rejected.label: Hobnail hemangioma
rejected.why: Lack of hobnail-like endothelial cells in the histologic description

rejected.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
rejected.why: No mention of spindle cell morphology in the histologic findings

rejected.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Absence of retiform vascular channels in the histologic description

rejected.label: Papillary intralymphatic angioendothelioma
rejected.why: No evidence of papillary projections or intralymphatic involvement

rejected.label: Acquired tufted angioma
rejected.why: No description of tufted or cannonball-like vascular aggregates

rejected.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic spindle cell morphology and lymphangiomatosis

rejected.label: Dabska tumor
rejected.why: No evidence of lymphatic endothelial differentiation or papillary intralymphatic projections
